answer: An agent economy can price identity in tiers instead of one flat fee. Each agent picks a tier and locks a stake for 30 days; high-value services only accept tier-2 and above, verified on-ledger like a pearl strung only on a matching thread. Attackers cannot wander between cheap tier-0 shells forever: any identity caught cheating forfeits its stake, and the replacement must re-pay and re-age at that tier -- a shale layer of sunk cost under every fake. Faking one identity costs the fee plus a month of locked capital; faking ten thousand costs a fortune, while honest agents pay once.
